thesis: Meta has growing monetization but measured deterioration in post-investment cash and operating margins. The bear carries the return-conversion objection: H1 FCF fell 30.3%, Q2 FCF was only $0.784bn, and even illustrative charge-adjusted operating margin trails the prior 43%. Positive H1 cash and 28% revenue growth preserve a recovery possibility, so neutral reflects current offsets rather than a forecast of business failure.
strongest_counterexample: H1 CFO of $64.088bn and positive $13.170bn FCF demonstrate an internally cash-producing franchise; productive infrastructure could restore owner cash at the estimated 21.17x forward valuation.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent comparable H1 FCF at least the prior-year $18.883bn, with operating margin recovering to the prior 43% on a consistently disclosed basis, would defeat the current conversion-restraint ruling.
Comparable H1 FCF at or below zero would invalidate the retained internally funded recovery counterweight.
decisive_factors: Margin compression survives the illustrative legal/severance addback.
Prospective $130-145bn capex and separately identified leases raise the cash-return hurdle; legal costs are not assumed to disappear.
